# AI-Human Map

This file records which parts of Auxid were written by people and which by AI, and names the AI model for each AI-written part. The numbers come from git history and are regenerated by [tools/authorship_map.py](tools/authorship_map.py). CI fails when they are out of date. This file was written by Claude Opus 5.5 and is not counted.

The OS layer is `auxid.time`, `auxid.env`, `auxid.ipc`, `auxid.proc`, `auxid.dl` and `auxid_win32.hpp`. Claude Fable 5 wrote almost all of it on 2026-08-26.

## How this is measured

- A commit counts as AI when its author is Claude or it has a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names an AI model. The model name comes from the trailer.
- Each line goes to the commit that last changed it: `git blame -w -M -C -C`, which ignores whitespace and follows moved and copied code back to its source.
- Blank lines and licence headers are left out, and so are `LICENSE`, the logo, vendored code, benchmark results and this file.

What it cannot show:

- A commit without a marker counts as human. Git cannot show AI help that left no marker.
- `bd49513` brought the module rewrite in from another repository as one commit. Its earlier history is not here, so it counts as human.
- It counts lines that survive. Human lines that AI later replaced are not shown, and an AI commit may include human edits.

As of `e35f587`, these types had no AI-written lines although their files have AI commits: `StringView`, `Hash`, `EqualTo`, `Group`, `BitMask`, `ProbeSeq`, `RefCounted`, `Mutex`, `LockGuard`, `ConditionVariable`, `MainThreadGuard`, the `Logger` declaration, and the test `Runner`, `TestRegistry` and `AutoRegister`.

## Keeping it current

1. Commit AI-written code with a trailer that names the exact model, for example `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. A tool name alone, such as "Copilot", fails the check. Don't mix human and AI work in one commit.
2. Run `python3 tools/authorship_map.py`. A library file that gains its first AI lines needs a short note in the "What the AI wrote" column. The script keeps notes that are already there, so update them by hand when they stop being true.
3. Commit `AI-Human-Map.md`. After AI-written commits this must be a separate commit, because a commit can't list its own hash. Human-only changes can include the map in the same commit.
4. Merge with a merge commit. Squashing or rebasing changes the commit hashes and can lose the trailers.

If an AI-written commit was merged with no marker or a vague one, add it to `RECORDED_BY_HAND` in the script and run it again.

If `main` moved while a pull request was open, merge `main` into it and run the script again.
